title: Light – Reflection and Refraction
seo_title: Light – Reflection and Refraction Class 10 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_code: Class 10, Chapter 9: Light – Reflection and Refraction
standard_text: Reflection of light by curved surfaces; images formed by spherical mirrors, centre of curvature, principal axis, principal focus, focal length, mirror formula (derivation not required), magnification. Refraction; laws of refraction, refractive index. Refraction of light by spherical lens; image formed by spherical lenses; lens formula (derivation not required); magnification. Power of a lens.

key_sub: Measure from the pole; with the light is +, against it is −.
body_html:
How to think about it

Use the New Cartesian sign convention: distances are measured from the pole (mirror) or optical centre (lens); distances in the direction of incident light are positive, against it negative. Objects are on the left, so u is negative. A concave mirror and a concave lens have negative focal lengths; a convex mirror and a convex lens have positive ones.

Mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, magnification m = −v/u. Lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, magnification m = v/u. Negative m means a real, inverted image. Power of a lens P = 1/f (f in metres), in dioptres. Refractive index n = c/v.

Example

Object at 30 cm from a concave mirror, f = 20 cm. Image?

u = −30, f = −20

1/v = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60

Answer: v = −60 cm (real, inverted, enlarged)

Example

Power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm?

f = +0.25 m

P = 1/0.25

Answer: +4 D

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting that u is negative.
  • Using the mirror formula for a lens.
  • Leaving f in centimetres when finding power.

faq.q: What is the New Cartesian sign convention?
faq.a: Distances are measured from the pole or optical centre; distances in the direction of incident light and heights above the axis are positive.

faq.q: What does the power of a lens tell us?
faq.a: How strongly it converges or diverges light: P = 1/f in dioptres; convex lenses have positive power.
